license_summary.fur_catcher_license: A fur catcher (trapping) license is required to take furbearing animals for commercial purposes (Code of Alabama §9-11-59). Fee amounts were not confirmed from an official source and are not listed here.
license_summary.trap_id: Each trap must be identified with a metal tag bearing the owner's name and address or Conservation ID number.
license_summary.bobcat_otter_tagging: Bobcat and otter fur/pelts must be tagged by a Division of Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries representative within 14 days of harvest and before sale or other disposal (licensed fur catchers may sell untagged to authorized resident fur dealers with a completed fur tag report).

verification.confirmation_notes: Ala. Admin. Code rules 220-2-.01, 220-2-.29, and 220-2-.30 read 2026-09-18 from the official Alabama Legislature admincode site, plus the Outdoor Alabama furbearer trapping page. Relative trapping dates converted to ISO and calendar-verified (Oct. 31, 2026 is the last Saturday of October 2026).
known_gaps: License fee amounts (§9-11-59) were not confirmed from an official source and are omitted; the license requirement itself is cited.
Nuisance/depredation take outside seasons is noted in license_summary but not modeled as a season; the app should offer a permit override rather than blocking the log.

Feral swine is listed as a fur-bearing animal in Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.30 but is intentionally excluded from this dataset under the project's documented exclusion rule (managed as a nuisance species under separate removal provisions, not in the furbearer trapping program). No take season is modeled for it.
